requirements.requirement: Create an SSH certificate authority on node1
requirements.summary: An ed25519 CA keypair was generated at /etc/ssh/ca/ssh_ca (private, 0600) and ssh_ca.pub (public, 0644), directly observed with fingerprint output and file listing.

requirements.requirement: Have the host present a certificate signed by that CA
requirements.summary: The ed25519 host public key was signed by the CA into ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub with principals node1 and its IP (10-year validity), verified via ssh-keygen -L. sshd_config was updated with a HostCertificate directive, sshd -t passed, sshd was reloaded, and an ssh -vv probe directly confirmed the server offers the signed certificate on the wire.

requirements.requirement: A client that trusts the authority connects without pinning the host key
requirements.summary: A client known_hosts file containing only an @cert-authority line (CA public key, no pinned host key) was used with StrictHostKeyChecking=yes and the connection succeeded ('CONNECTED_NO_PINNING'). A negative control with an empty known_hosts file (no CA trust) was rejected with 'Host key verification failed', confirming the success stemmed from CA trust rather than a pre-existing pinned key or lax checking.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id 1f0657c2... with sshd active and cert/CA files present (cmd-dd68aa4528014129), matching the global before_prepare boot-identity snapshot. A backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' returned control before disconnect (cmd-9de7c83ebbeb4db1). Polling showed connection refused then success (cmd-ba5b3bc0ba16409f, cmd-2f97b8aaa6fc4888), and boot_id changed to 5c821d10... post-restart (cmd-460664733fda409c), consistent with the global after_executor snapshot. sshd, cert files, and the HostCertificate config line were confirmed intact, and a fresh end-to-end CA-trust connection test succeeded after reboot (cmd-d3e836433aea41cd), demonstrating full recovery.

overall_summary: The executor created an SSH host CA on node1, signed the ed25519 host key into a certificate, configured sshd to present it, and directly demonstrated both a successful client connection trusting only the CA (no pinned host key) and a rejected connection without CA trust — satisfying the full task contract with direct on-wire evidence. The mandatory node-restart protocol was also completed with a full pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and a fresh post-restart connection test confirming the certificate trust and configuration survived the reboot. All temporary test artifacts were cleaned up and no unnecessary or risky mutations were left in place.
limitations: The after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare (prepare was disabled for this task), so preparer-vs-executor separation relies solely on the before_prepare/after_executor comparison, which is otherwise consistent and sufficient here.
Captured stdout for some commands may be head-truncated (e.g., sshd -V usage banner), but this does not affect any material outcome.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all 21 executor commands chronologically. One early mutation attempt (cmd-613dfcadf4f146df, mkdir without sudo) failed with permission denied and caused no state change — a benign discovery step, not a troubleshooting mutation. Temporary test SSH keypairs and authorized_keys/known_hosts entries added for the positive/negative connection tests (cmd-fe12e8534f1a4f7c) were fully removed afterward (cmd-65f1208cbe784c02), leaving authorized_keys at its original line count (1). The mandatory reboot (cmd-9de7c83ebbeb4db1) is a required part of the restart-evidence protocol, was bounded, and node1 recovered cleanly. A second temporary test keypair used for post-restart verification (cmd-d3e836433aea41cd) was likewise fully cleaned up (cmd-01fa15f3c8604cc2), confirmed by authorized_keys returning to 1 line. The after_executor temp-file diff only shows systemd-private directories tied to the timesyncd/hostnamed services across the reboot boundary, not executor-created residue. No unnecessary, retained, or destructive mutations were found; no unsafe exposure or weakened security controls were introduced.
